mods.name: DeathLogger
mods.description: Keeps a log of your deaths with the cause, location, inventory and a screenshot, and can restore a lost inventory.

releases.notes:
DeathLogger 1.1.0 for Minecraft 1.21.1 on NeoForge. This version was made for Tesseract, who asked for a 1.21.1 build.

It has the same features as [1.1.0 for 26.3](https://github.com/pamquale/DeathLogger/releases/tag/1.1.0): a log for each world and server, restore and delete that ask first, permission nodes for the server commands, death screenshots, and shulker box and bundle previews.

## Differences from the 26.3 version

- NeoForge only.
- The permission nodes `deathlogger.list`, `deathlogger.view`, `deathlogger.restore` and `deathlogger.delete` go through NeoForge's PermissionAPI. Without a permission mod the commands need permission level 4.
- With Better Statistics Screen 3.x installed, its menu bar gets a DeathLogger button.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 1.21.1 and Java 21
- NeoForge 21.1

The source is on the [`1.21.1` branch](https://github.com/pamquale/DeathLogger/tree/1.21.1).

Based on [DeathLog](https://github.com/gliscowo/deathlog) by glisco03.

releases.notes:
DeathLogger 1.1.0 for Minecraft 26.3, on Fabric, NeoForge and Forge.

## Changes since 1.0.0

- Updated for Minecraft 26.3. Builds for 26.1 and 26.2 stay on the 1.0.0 release.
- Each singleplayer world gets its own log. 1.0.0 wrote every world into one shared log, which is kept and opens from an "Older deaths" button.
- Server logs are named after the server address, so two servers with the same name in your list no longer share a log.
- Restore and Delete ask first. Restore is disabled where it can't work, with a tooltip saying why, and a restored entry shows when and by whom.
- Items the game can't read, for example from a mod you removed, keep their slot and come back when the mod does.
- Logs store the game's data version, and stored items are upgraded when Minecraft changes their format.
- 0.4.x logs are converted to the current format. The original file is kept as `<name>.r3.bak`.
- Deleting an entry also deletes its screenshot, and screenshots are saved at a smaller size.
- Legacy death detection no longer records each death twice.
- The key binding has its own DeathLogger category under Controls.
- NeoForge and Forge servers with DeathLogger accept players who don't have it, vanilla clients included.
- Deaths that another mod cancels, such as revive or grave mods, are no longer recorded.
- Permission mods can grant the commands separately through the nodes `deathlogger.list`, `deathlogger.view`, `deathlogger.restore` and `deathlogger.delete`. Without one, permission level 4 is still required.
- On a LAN world, guests can no longer see or restore the host's deaths.
- A screenshot name sent by a server could make the client read other image files on disk. Only DeathLogger's own file names are accepted now.
- Very large logs or entries could disconnect an operator using `/deathlogger view`. The view now sends what fits and says how much was left out.

## Requirements

Minecraft 26.3 and Java 25. On Fabric you also need Fabric API.

Based on [DeathLog](https://github.com/gliscowo/deathlog) by glisco03.

releases.notes:
DeathLogger 1.0.0 is a rewrite of [DeathLog](https://github.com/gliscowo/deathlog) by glisco03 as a Fabric, NeoForge and Forge mod, with a new storage format, networking, GUI and build. The data model and much of the design still come from DeathLog.

## Supported versions

| Minecraft | Fabric | NeoForge | Forge |
| :-- | :--: | :--: | :--: |
| 26.2 | yes | yes | no |
| 26.1.2 | yes | yes | yes |
| 26.1.1 | yes | yes | no |
| 26.1 | yes | yes | no |

Forge is only built for 26.1.2. Forge has no recommended build for 26.1 or 26.1.1, and those versions crash on startup even with no mods installed.

## Changes since 0.4.3

- Runs on NeoForge and Forge as well as Fabric.
- owo-lib is no longer needed. Logs are saved with vanilla codecs, the GUI uses vanilla widgets, the config is plain JSON and networking uses vanilla payloads.
- Death screenshots are taken at the moment of death and saved under the entry's own name.
- Shulker box and bundle contents are shown in the detail panel.
- The copied /give command includes the item's components, so enchantments and shulker contents come along.
- The detail panel scrolls, so long entries fit.
- The key binding is unset by default. Open the log from the Statistics screen, from Better Statistics Screen's menu bar, or bind a key yourself.

Logs now use format revision 4. A 0.4.x log (revision 3) is renamed to `<name>.r3.bak` and a new log is started, because this version has no converter.

## Requirements

Java 25, which Minecraft 26.1 and later ship with. On Fabric you also need Fabric API.

releases.notes:
DeathLogger 0.4.2 for Minecraft 1.21.4, an updated version of [DeathLog](https://github.com/gliscowo/deathlog) by glisco03, maintained by pamquale.

## What's new

- Updated for Minecraft 1.21.4.
- The detail view scrolls, for deaths with a lot of information.
- Your death screenshot is shown in the log details.
- Shulker box and bundle contents are shown in the detail panel, no hovering needed.
- With BetterStats installed, its menu has a "Deaths" button that opens DeathLogger.

releases.notes:
DeathLogger for Minecraft 1.21.11 on Fabric, with a new BetterStats integration and a set of bug fixes.

## Requirements

- Fabric Loader
- Fabric API 0.141.3 or newer
- owo-lib 0.13.0 or newer

## BetterStats

BetterStats 5.x gets a "View Death Log" entry in its View menu. It works with BetterStats 5.0.x and 5.1.x. The old integration crashed the game when BetterStats 5 was installed.

## Fixes

- All UI text showed raw translation keys (`text.deathlogger.*`) because the language files didn't load.
- The server-side death log stopped saving for good if any stray file ended up in `deaths/`.
- Joining a world with a corrupted or incompatible death log crashed the client. It shows an error toast now.
- Serverbound packet handlers check bounds and nulls, so a bad restore, delete or info request can't throw on the server.
- `/deathlogger view` sent the full inventory of every death in one packet. Inventories are now fetched when you open an entry.
- The DeathLogger button covered the tab headers on the vanilla statistics screen. It sits in the bottom-left corner now.
- The death counter didn't update after deleting an entry.
- Deleting for a profile with no deaths, or opening the screen with no storage, threw a NullPointerException.
- Added the missing pt_BR translations.

readmeSummary: DeathLogger keeps a log of every time you die: when and how it happened, where you were, your level, everything you were carrying and, optionally, a screenshot of the moment.
